text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- Opposition Pakistan People's Party staged a walk-out from the Natioanal Assembly in protest against the attitude of the Speaker and accused treasury benches of bulldozing bills.
- Prisoners at Aidala Jail near Islamabad continued a hunger strike in protest against Saturday's jail riot in which more than 100 inmates and policemen were injured.
- Pakistan People's Party denies report that Benazir Bhutto was seeking asylum in Britain.
THE NATION

- A three-member team of International Monetary Fund arrived on Monday to hold talks for financial assistance to Pakistan under Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility and to review the massive economic programme of the present government.
- Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) probes corruption allegations against the former managing director Pakistan Television Rana Sheikh.
- Prime Minister Mian Nawaz Sharif rang Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani with condolences after 2,400 people were killing in an earthquake in Khorasan province.
DAWN
- The prime ministers of Pakistan and India agreed to set up joint working groups to resolve all outstanding issues, including the Kashmir dispute, officials said.
- Pakistan has sought expert advice of the International Monetary Fund to revamp the tax machinery and remove fiscal anomalies to improve the "highly alarming revenue position", sources said.
- Food and Agriculture Minister Abida Hussain told the Senate (upper house) that 2.383 million tons of wheat worth $451 million was imported from the United States in fiscal 1996/97 (July-June).
- The trade deficit in the first 10 months of 1996/97 (July-June) reached $2.89 billion, compared to $2.86 billion in the year-ago period, the Federal Bureau of Statistics said.
- The consumer price index rose 11.45 percent in April year-on-year, the Federal Bureau of Statistics said.
- The Pakistan Society of Sugar Technologists said there was no immediate threat of a sugar shortage.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government turned down a proposal to offer bad debts of state-run commercial banks and financial institutions to a foreign debt recovery company at a 50 percent discount.
- The All Pakistan Textile Mills Association has proposed setting up a textile ministry and has asked for 53 billion rupees to meet the sector's working capital needs.
- The state-run Sui Southern Gas Company is seeking government assistance to recover three billion rupees from influential consumers.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
